about: Which of the Masses the rubrics permit the FSSP's ordo offers, and which it prints first, as read from the seminary's 2026 page (fsspolgs.org/liturgical-calendar, read 2026-11-09). The page is a list kept by hand: where it puts first a Mass no rule here gives, the day is listed in test/fixtures/fssp-2026-masses.json. To be confirmed against the printed Liturgical Ordo & FSSP Directory.

first.about: The Mass printed first, when the day allows it; otherwise the Mass of the day. Rules are tried in order.

rules.source: 3 to 7 November 2026: the Daily Mass for the Dead first on every 4th class day, also on the first Friday and Saturday; second on St. Charles Borromeo, a 3rd class feast.

First Thursday, Friday and Saturday of 2026: the votive Mass first on a feria (2 January, 4 September, 1 October, 5 December) and on a Saturday of Our Lady (3 January, 4 July, 1 August), second on every 3rd class feast.

omit.about: Masses the rubrics permit that the page never prints.

masses.source: The daily Mass for the dead outside the octave of All Souls (no. 423).
The first Thursday, Friday and Saturday votive Masses on the ferias of Lent and Passiontide: none in 2026 (5 to 7 March). No. 384 permits them on any day of the 3rd class.

massesForCertainPlaces.about: Masses 'pro aliquibus locis' the page offers on a 4th class day. They are not in the universal calendar, the United States proper or the Fraternity's (data/layers/fssp.json): the French district's monthly ordo (fssp.fr/ordo-du-mois) prints a plain feria on 8 May (2020, 2023, 2025), 6 July (2020, 2023), 27 June (2023) and 4 July (2023, 2024), and the Institute of Christ the King lists the 8 May Masses as alternatives to the feria. They are offered as Masses of a saint in the Martyrology or of Our Lady, which a 4th class day admits (nos. 302c, 303b, 309b, 388). 'commemoratedOnThePage': the page also commemorates the Mass in the row of the day's own Mass; that is not followed (test/fixtures/fssp-2026-differences.json).
toConfirm: The titles in Latin and Spanish, and the colours, against the Missal's Masses for certain places.
The date of All Holy Popes, printed on 4 July 2026.
